chapter: Southern Illinois roadhouse and St. Louis
title: The five-piece roadhouse band and its music
summary: The roadhouse band had drums, bass, piano and banjo; the players knew nothing of New Orleans but played tunes like Dinah and Sand.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: What kind of band was that?

We got a band of five pieces. I think it was a guy named Jap(?)...Jap(?) Palmer, they called him, and a guy named Baker playing piano. Jap Palmer was a drummer. We had drums, a bass, there was a piano player, and Jap -- we didn't have a trumpet. We had a guitar player or a banjo player, and I played banjo or guitar.
This music must have been... I don't want to put words in your mouth. But was this music different from the music you had been playing in Baton Rouge and...?
Oh yeah. It was altogether different, really.
Did you care that it was different, or was it just...?

It was always a different combination. I always played like I played in Baton Rouge. But it seemed to me that I was working with a different class of musicians. Because none of these guys at that time was from

New Orleans. They didn't know nothin' about New Orleans. But they practically played the same tunes, like "Dinah" and "Sand"... It was practically the same thing, but naturally you didn't have those combos, the full combos like you had... I can't remember a trombonist we had... You couldn't find a good trombone player.
